data.narrative:
Quilter is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Sergiy Nesterenko that has raised $15M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public entity (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage band, including peers such as Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $15M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement to next-stage financing, yielding $30M. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B (range $1.1B–$2.0B), reflecting the broader market for robotics capital intensity and growth expectations. The spread between these two methods reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation conventions in frontier tech.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $26M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $840M. The wide dispersion—spanning nearly two orders of magnitude—reflects tension between stage-appropriate early-stage advancement (favoring the low end) and peer comparables that skew toward later-stage, higher-valued robotics firms. Key uncertainties include Quilter's unit economics relative to the peer set, capital efficiency to next milestone, and whether peer valuations reflect justified market conditions or sector enthusiasm. Stage definition and revenue traction would materially narrow this band.
